title: Lemmatization, Morphological Analysis & Historical POS Tagging
query: How do computational toolkits like CLTK, Morpheus, and TreeTagger perform morphological tagging and lemmatization on historical language corpora compared to LLM-based parsing and manual lexicon lookups?

results.title: A pilot study for BERT language modelling and morphological analysis for ancient and medieval Greek
results.authors_venue_year: A pilot study for BERT language modelling and morphological analysis for ancient and medieval GreekP Singh, G Rutten, E Lefever - … of the 5th Joint SIGHUM Workshop …, 2021 - aclanthology.orgExplains that Morpheus, a rule-based system, provides all possible morphological analyses but does not disambiguate the correct one, struggles with unknown words or non-classical Greek forms, and is not scoped for Byzantine Greek.Historical Variation Challenges: Notes that the rule-based nature of Morpheus does not handle historical and dialectal variation well, specifically struggling with words that change conjugation or declension, although its morphological information is fundamental to many Ancient Greek analyses.BERT Model Performance: Demonstrates that a novel subword-based BERT language model fine-tuned for morphological analysis is more flexible for analyzing irregular forms and performs better on Greek that is not from the classical period, unlike many existing taggers that rely on Morpheus.Save Cite Cited by 88 Related articles All 9 versions  No full text available View as HTML [PDF] aclanthology.org

results.title: Lemmatisation of Medieval Greek: Against the Limits of Transformer's Capabilities?
results.authors_venue_year: Lemmatisation of Medieval Greek: Against the Limits of Transformer's Capabilities?C Swaelens, P Singh, I De Vos… - Proceedings of the 2024 …, 2024 - aclanthology.orgReviews the development and structure of rule-based systems like Morpheus and statistical models like TreeTagger for morphological analysis and lemmatization of Classical Greek and other historical languages.CLTK Components: Details the components of the Classical Language Toolkit (CLTK), which includes two lemmatizers for Classical Greek: a Stanza-based algorithm and a back-off lemmatizer combining dictionary lookups, unigram models, and rule-based methods (including elements from Morpheus).Performance Comparison: Compares the performance of existing lemmatization algorithms for Classical Greek to transformer-based approaches on unedited Byzantine Greek, noting a substantial accuracy drop (around 30 percentage points) for existing algorithms due to orthographic inconsistencies.Save Cite Cited by 6 Related articles All 4 versions  View as HTML Check for full text @ X

results.title: Exploring large language models for classical philology
results.authors_venue_year: Exploring large language models for classical philologyF Riemenschneider, A Frank - … of the 61st Annual Meeting of the …, 2023 - aclanthology.orgCompares the performance of new LLM-based models (specifically T5 models) against the Classical Language Toolkit (CLTK) and UDPipe for lemmatization.Standard Tool Morpheus: Mentions Morpheus as the standard tool for Ancient Greek morphological analysis, which enabled direct comparison of models and produced strong models for Latin.LLM Performance Improvements: Demonstrates that tri-lingual LLMs outperform existing systems on PoS tagging and lemmatization, implying better performance than traditional rule-based or statistical methods for these tasks on Ancient Greek.Save Cite Cited by 90 Related articles All 6 versions  No full text available View as HTML [PDF] researchsquare.com

results.title: Digital tools applied on Ancient Greek texts
results.authors_venue_year: [PDF][PDF] Digital tools applied on Ancient Greek textsM Kritikou, KL Kermanidis - 2026 - assets-eu.researchsquare.comExplains that the CLTK lemmatizer uses TreeTagger for Part-of-Speech (PoS) assignment on annotated Ancient Greek corpora before determining the appropriate lemma, which improves the disambiguation of forms corresponding to multiple lemmas and different PoS categories.Morpheus Integration: Notes that the Digital Fragmenta Historicorum Graecorum (DFHG) includes tools and linkages to external lexical resources such as Morpheus, which helps in the analysis of historical Greek texts.Manual vs. GLEM: Mentions that lemmatizers like GLEM assist scholars by uncovering statistical patterns in the Greek language that were previously missed in manual research.Save Cite Related articles  View as HTML [PDF] brill.com

results.title: Lemmatization for ancient greek: An experimental assessment of the state of the art
results.authors_venue_year: Lemmatization for ancient greek: An experimental assessment of the state of the artA Vatri, B McGillivray - Journal of Greek linguistics, 2020 - brill.comCompares the accuracy of the CLTK lemmatizer, CLTK backoff lemmatizer, GLEM, and lemmatizations from the Diorisis corpus and the Lemmatized Ancient Greek Texts repository using blinded evaluation by highly proficient readers of Ancient Greek.Reliability of Lemmatization Methods: Suggests that lemmatization methods incorporating large lexica and part-of-speech tagging, like the Diorisis corpus and the CLTK backoff lemmatizer, are more dependable than methods relying primarily on machine learning and smaller lexica.Incorporates Morpheus Lexicon: Utilizes a dictionary-based lemmatizer that includes the Morpheus lexicon in its chain mechanism for disambiguation, showing how lexicon lookups are incorporated into toolkits.Save Cite Cited by 33 Related articles All 5 versions  [PDF] studiesaggilinguistici.it

results.title: Ensemble lemmatization with the classical language toolkit
results.authors_venue_year: Ensemble lemmatization with the classical language toolkitPJ Burns - Studi e Saggi Linguistici, 2020 - studiesaggilinguistici.itIntroduces the Classical Language Toolkit (CLTK) as an open-source Python package that provides a non-standard solution, specifically the Ensemble lemmatizer, for historical language lemmatization and NLP research.Methodology Comparison: Explains that CLTK's Ensemble lemmatizer, which is a series of sub-lemmatizers deployed in unison, contrasts with lexicon-based approaches by allowing an unlimited number of lexicons, rule definitions, or tagging strategies to be combined for optimal lemma choice.Integrating Existing Tools: Mentions that off-the-shelf tools like Morpheus and language-independent tools like TreeTagger are available for Latin, but CLTK's approach allows their wrappers to be chained together as sub-lemmatizers to leverage their combined strengths in a single workflow.Save Cite Cited by 12 Related articles All 2 versions  No full text available View as HTML Check for full text @ X

results.title: On the implementation of Latin part-of-speech taggers in intertextuality analysis: TreeTagger, CLTK, Cracovia system, LatinCy, and ChatGPT compared
results.authors_venue_year: On the implementation of Latin part-of-speech taggers in intertextuality analysis: TreeTagger, CLTK, Cracovia system, LatinCy, and ChatGPT comparedM Wittweiler, F Schropp, TE Konrad… - … Scholarship in the …, 2025 - academic.oup.comCompares the performance of the Classical Language Toolkit (CLTK), the TreeTagger, LatinCy, the Cracovia system, and ChatGPT for Latin Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging to refine filtering for intertextuality analysis in ancient texts.Evaluates Tool Accuracy: Found that the Cracovia system, which uses transformer-based machine learning, surpassed other taggers by approximately 2 percentage points in accuracy, with the older, probabilistic-based TreeTagger also demonstrating competitive performance.Assesses LLM Performance: Notes that GPT-4, while showing remarkable results, still lags behind the state-of-the-art specialized taggers for Latin POS, suggesting that LLMs are not yet superior for this specific task in historical languages.Save Cite Cited by 1 Related articles All 5 versions  [PDF] ajosr.org

results.title: Comparative Evaluation of Latin Natural Language Processing Tools for Pedagogical Applications
results.authors_venue_year: [PDF][PDF] Comparative Evaluation of Latin Natural Language Processing Tools for Pedagogical ApplicationsA Han - 2026 - ajosr.orgCompares five prominent Latin NLP systems, including transformer-based models (LatinBERT), rule-based morphological analyzers (LemLat 3.0), and Universal Dependencies pipelines (Stanza, LatinCy), across architecture, training data, and task performance, which addresses the comparison of LLM-based parsing and manual lexicon lookups against other toolkits.Describes Rule-Based Systems: Indicates that rule-based systems, such as LemLat 3.0, rely on extensive curated lexical databases and hand-encoded morphological rules derived from classical grammar to map word forms to candidate lemmas, reflecting the approach of manual lexicon lookups.Evaluates Model Strengths: Notes that transformer-based models demonstrate strong contextual understanding and high accuracy in disambiguation tasks, while rule-based systems offer reliability for vocabulary learning, suggesting different strengths compared to LLM-based parsing.Save Cite Related articles  View as HTML [PDF] aclanthology.org

results.title: Improving lemmatization of non-standard languages with joint learning
results.authors_venue_year: Improving lemmatization of non-standard languages with joint learningE Manjavacas, Á Kádár… - Proceedings of the 2019 …, 2019 - aclanthology.orgPresents an encoder-decoder architecture enriched with sentence context information and a hierarchical sentence encoder for lemmatization as a string-transduction task.Improved Performance: Shows that the proposed architecture, which uses a joint bidirectional language model loss, significantly improves lemmatization performance on non-standard historical languages over the state-of-the-art.No Morphological Annotation Required: Emphasizes that the neural architecture does not require Part-of-Speech or morphological annotations, which is an advantage over some existing tools for historical corpora.Save Cite Cited by 94 Related articles All 5 versions  No full text available View as HTML Looking for more results...Scholar Labs is currently not designed for queries like this.Suggestions:Try a different questionTry your query on Google ScholarNo results found.Search stopped.Looking for results...Scholar Labs is currently not designed for queries like this.Suggestions:Try a different questionTry your query on Google ScholarNo results found.Search stopped.An error occurred.RetryMore resultsReady to explore your own questions and answers?Ask your questionScholar Labs is experimental and can make mistakes.Help & PrivacyPrivacyTermsHelpYou're on the waitlistScholar Labs home
